summary: Evaluated replacing the hand-rolled markdown extraction in the auto-fetch floor with marked's token stream and found it NOT viable on all four axes, with numbers: availability (marked is declared nowhere in package.json and reaches this checkout only as a transitive dependency of the optional @opentui/core, so an import in the mandatory floor can throw at module load), performance (Lexer.lex is 5093x slower than the detector on a 200 KB bracket run and 3810x slower on a 400 KB `![` run, trading one denial-of-service surface for a larger one), span mapping (tokens carry no offsets, raw concatenation drifts on CRLF, and token.href is empty for the tab-in-scheme vector T24 F-004 closed and loses a backslash on the T24R2#F-001 class), and correctness (12 of 14 coverage rows the floor flags are not resolved to an image by marked, so adoption would release them). Closed the three blockers and three majors by hand instead, removing the invented bounds rather than adding one: image-inside-a-link is now covered in every spelling by the CommonMark alt-text/content asymmetry; MAX_REFERENCE_LABEL is deleted and replaced by an exact necessary condition derived from the document's own definition table; the inline destination grammar is gated on an indexed `)` and memoised by description end, taking the reviewer's cubic 12.5 KB shape from 516829.3 ms to 0.7 ms; srcset candidates are split on the decoded value; reference labels are normalised with CommonMark whitespace collapse on both sides; and the completeness sentence in policies.md is corrected and now verifies in both directions.

changed_files.change: Closed T72#F-001 by applying CommonMark's alt-text/content asymmetry: an image construct's description is still skipped, a link construct's description is scanned and only its destination span is skipped, in both markdown passes. Deleted MAX_REFERENCE_LABEL and the REFERENCE_LABEL regex, replacing the bound with an exact necessary condition (non-whitespace prefix counts against the longest key the document's own reference definitions produced) and skipping the reference pass entirely when the document defines no labels. Indexed `)` positions alongside the brackets and gated INLINE_DESTINATION on a binary search for one, and memoised both the destination reading and the SENSITIVE_URL_VALUE test by description end, which removes the quadratic and cubic shapes. Added a per-span dedupe for inline findings. Split the srcset candidate list on the decoded value when decoding reveals a comma the raw bytes do not carry, masking the whole raw attribute value in that case. Normalised reference labels with CommonMark's trim/collapse/fold rule identically at the definition and use sites. Extracted isExfilDestination from considerUrl. Rewrote the module header's covered list, its matching rules, and the false performance claim, and recorded which oracle settles which question (T72#F-008).

Added seven tests, all written before the corresponding production code and all RED on the pre-fix detector: an image inside a link in seven spellings plus the image-in-image and click-gated controls; reference labels at 998/999/1000/1200/4096 characters in three forms plus the undefined-label negatives; CommonMark whitespace collapse on both sides plus non-whitespace negatives; the entity-encoded srcset comma under a non-empty allowlist plus the allowlist and raw-comma controls; a nine-shape performance budget covering the reviewer's pathological inputs and the shapes this change makes newly reachable; and T77_CLASS_VECTORS driven through prepareOutputForPersistence and validateOutputForTransport, with AC5's public-link and local-badge rows re-pinned. No existing test was modified, weakened or removed.

Auto-fetch subsection only, plus the Version line (0.1.3 -> 0.1.4). The covered list now names the image-nested-in-a-link case with the README badge idiom as its carrier; a new sentence states that what a markdown link does not cover is the navigation rather than its content, and that an image inside another image's description is alt text and is not a finding; and the matching paragraph now states the srcset decoding rule, CommonMark label matching with case folding and whitespace collapse applied to both sides, and that there is no label-length bound at all, the only criterion being whether the document defines the label.
